### Transformer blocks, positions and encoder/decoder tasks

Connect transformer internals to the model interfaces used in embedding, classification and text generation.

**Priority:** Foundation · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [Queries, keys, values, masks and multi-head attention](dl.md#dl-attention-math) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Residual and feed-forward sublayers:** A transformer block combines attention, residual paths, normalisation and a position-wise feed-forward network.
  - Example: Print the shape after every sublayer of a tiny block and verify the residual addition dimensions.
  - Videos:
    - [Build GPT from scratch, in code](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kCc8FmEb1nY) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Language modeling, embeddings, causal attention, transformer blocks and sampling.
      - Useful because: Trace token IDs to logits and understand a small end-to-end transformer.
      - Watch for: Focus on residual and feed-forward sublayers. Then reproduce the lesson example: Print the shape after every sublayer of a tiny block and verify the residual addition dimensions.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on residual and feed-forward sublayers. Then reproduce the lesson example: Print the shape after every sublayer of a tiny block and verify the residual addition dimensions.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Position information:** Attention alone does not encode token order; absolute or relative positional mechanisms provide order information.
  - Example: Compare token embeddings before and after adding sinusoidal positions to the same permuted sequence.
  - Videos:
    - [Build GPT from scratch, in code](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kCc8FmEb1nY) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture

- [ ] **Encoder, decoder and cross-attention:** Encoders commonly use bidirectional context; causal decoders predict continuations; cross-attention reads a separate source representation.
  - Example: Sketch masks for sentence embedding, autoregressive generation and sequence-to-sequence translation.
  - Videos:

  - Example: For [A,B,C,D], train inputs [A,B,C] against targets [B,C,D].

### Causal convolutions, dilation and hierarchical sequence models

Compare recurrent, convolutional and attention-based sequence processing using explicit context boundaries.

**Priority:** Specialization · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [Convolutions, padding, stride, dilation and pooling](dl.md#dl-convolution-arithmetic) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **One-dimensional channel layout:** Conv1d commonly uses batch, channels, length, whereas token embeddings are often stored as batch, length, features.
  - Example: Transpose a B,T,D embedding tensor to B,D,T before a sequence convolution.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Building makemore Part 5: WaveNet](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3YJ5hKiMQ0) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 56m
      - Explains: A hierarchical sequence model and the engineering of multidimensional tensor operations.
      - Useful because: Extend a tiny character model while recording tensor shapes; the video distinguishes its implementation from dilated convolutions.
      - Watch for: Focus on one-dimensional channel layout. Then reproduce the lesson example: Transpose a B,T,D embedding tensor to B,D,T before a sequence convolution.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on one-dimensional channel layout. Then reproduce the lesson example: Transpose a B,T,D embedding tensor to B,D,T before a sequence convolution.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Causal padding:** A causal convolution must not read a future position; ordinary symmetric padding can leak later tokens.
  - Example: Left-pad a toy sequence and assert that changing its final value leaves earlier outputs unchanged.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Building makemore Part 5: WaveNet](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3YJ5hKiMQ0) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 56m
      - Explains: A hierarchical sequence model and the engineering of multidimensional tensor operations.

- [ ] **Dilation:** Dilated kernels space their input positions apart, expanding the receptive field without increasing kernel element count.
  - Example: Trace which input indices influence one output for kernel size three and dilation two.
  - Videos:
    - [Karpathy — Building makemore Part 5: WaveNet](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3YJ5hKiMQ0) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture · 56m

## Representation and generative learning

<a id="dl-representation-learning"></a>

### Embeddings, contrastive learning and metric losses

Learn why an embedding space must match the downstream similarity task and evaluation setup.

**Priority:** Specialization · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [MSE, binary and multiclass cross-entropy](dl.md#dl-losses) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Learned embedding tables:** An embedding lookup selects trainable rows rather than computing a meaningful representation from the integer ID itself.
  - Example: Train a tiny token table and show that renumbering tokens consistently does not change the task.
  - Videos:
    - [Neural Networks Part 11: Word Embedding and Word2Vec](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=viZrOnJclY0) · StatQuest · Josh Starmer · Focused explanation
      - Explains: A visual, step-by-step explanation of the topic named in the title.
      - Useful because: Use the worked intuition before writing the corresponding small experiment.
      - Watch for: Focus on learned embedding tables. Then reproduce the lesson example: Train a tiny token table and show that renumbering tokens consistently does not change the task.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://statquest.org/video_index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on learned embedding tables. Then reproduce the lesson example: Train a tiny token table and show that renumbering tokens consistently does not change the task.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Cosine and Euclidean distance:** Distance choices interact with vector norms; normalised vectors make cosine and dot-product rankings agree.
  - Example: Compare the nearest neighbours before and after normalising synthetic vectors with different magnitudes.
  - Videos:
    - [Neural Networks Part 11: Word Embedding and Word2Vec](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=viZrOnJclY0) · StatQuest · Josh Starmer · Focused explanation
      - Explains: A visual, step-by-step explanation of the topic named in the title.
      - Useful because: Use the worked intuition before writing the corresponding small experiment.

      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.

- [ ] **Positive and negative pairs:** Contrastive training requires a meaningful rule for related and unrelated examples; false negatives can damage learning.
  - Example: Construct two augmented views of one generated shape as a positive pair and document possible false negatives.
  - Videos:
    - [Neural Networks Part 11: Word Embedding and Word2Vec](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=viZrOnJclY0) · StatQuest · Josh Starmer · Focused explanation
      - Explains: A visual, step-by-step explanation of the topic named in the title.
      - Useful because: Use the worked intuition before writing the corresponding small experiment.

- [ ] **Triplet margin:** A triplet loss penalises an anchor whose positive is not closer than its negative by a chosen margin.

### Autoencoders, latent spaces and variational objectives

Distinguish reconstruction from probabilistic generation before choosing an anomaly or generation method.

**Priority:** Specialization · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [MSE, binary and multiclass cross-entropy](dl.md#dl-losses) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Encoder and decoder bottlenecks:** An autoencoder compresses and reconstructs inputs; a useful bottleneck restricts what can be copied.
  - Example: Train a 20-to-2-to-20 network on generated vectors and inspect reconstruction error.
  - Videos:
    - [MIT 6.S191 (2025) — Deep Generative Modeling](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SdTZAMDKrNY) · MIT · Ava Amini · University lecture
      - Explains: Latent representations and major generative model families.
      - Useful because: Use the conceptual overview with the written derivations; required practice uses toy distributions.
      - Watch for: Focus on encoder and decoder bottlenecks. Then reproduce the lesson example: Train a 20-to-2-to-20 network on generated vectors and inspect reconstruction error.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://introtodeeplearning.com/2025/index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on encoder and decoder bottlenecks. Then reproduce the lesson example: Train a 20-to-2-to-20 network on generated vectors and inspect reconstruction error.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Denoising reconstruction:** A denoising model receives corrupted inputs and learns a clean target; corruption must resemble the intended use case.
  - Example: Add Gaussian noise to generated waveforms and reconstruct the clean signal.

#### Lab: Autoencoders, latent spaces and variational objectives

Build a tiny CPU denoising autoencoder for generated sine waves. Add a two-dimensional variational bottleneck, plot reconstruction and KL terms separately, and describe why reconstruction error alone does not prove anomaly-detection quality.

**Deliverables**

- Runnable code or notebook with a small reproducible input
- README explaining decisions, results and limitations

**Completion checks**

- [ ] Build a tiny CPU denoising autoencoder for generated sine waves. Add a two-dimensional variational bottleneck, plot reconstruction and KL terms separately, and describe why reconstruction error alone does not prove anomaly-detection quality.
- [ ] Include at least one happy-path and one failure/edge-case check; explain the output using the concept checklist.

### GAN and diffusion mechanics on toy distributions

Compare adversarial and denoising generation objectives without needing large image models or paid compute.

**Priority:** Specialization · **Study:** 4h · **Practice:** 5h

**Prerequisites:** [Autoencoders, latent spaces and variational objectives](dl.md#dl-autoencoders-vae) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Adversarial objectives:** A generator and discriminator optimise different objectives in an interacting process; improving one loss does not guarantee better samples.
  - Example: Fit a generator to points from two Gaussian clusters and inspect whether both clusters appear.
  - Videos:
    - [MIT 6.S191 (2025) — Deep Generative Modeling](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SdTZAMDKrNY) · MIT · Ava Amini · University lecture
      - Explains: Latent representations and major generative model families.
      - Useful because: Use the conceptual overview with the written derivations; required practice uses toy distributions.
      - Watch for: Focus on adversarial objectives. Then reproduce the lesson example: Fit a generator to points from two Gaussian clusters and inspect whether both clusters appear.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.

      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.

      - Watch for: Focus on adversarial objectives. Then reproduce the lesson example: Fit a generator to points from two Gaussian clusters and inspect whether both clusters appear.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Alternating updates and detach:** Discriminator training uses generated examples without updating the generator; generator training must preserve its gradient path.
  - Example: Check parameter changes after each half-step and catch an accidental generator detach during its own update.
  - Videos:

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Mode collapse:** A generator can produce only a subset of the data distribution while fooling a limited discriminator.
  - Example: Measure coverage of both toy clusters rather than showing only a few appealing samples.

## Diagnostics and efficiency

<a id="dl-training-diagnostics"></a>

### Overfit one batch, diagnose loss and debug numerical failures

Locate implementation problems before spending time on bigger models or long training runs.

**Priority:** Foundation · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [PyTorch loops, checkpoints and reproducibility](dl.md#dl-training-loop) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Overfit a tiny batch:** A sufficiently flexible model should reduce the loss of a small consistent training set; failure often signals a pipeline or optimisation bug.
  - Example: Disable regularisation and fit eight generated labelled examples before training on a larger dataset.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.
      - Watch for: Focus on overfit a tiny batch. Then reproduce the lesson example: Disable regularisation and fit eight generated labelled examples before training on a larger dataset.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on overfit a tiny batch. Then reproduce the lesson example: Disable regularisation and fit eight generated labelled examples before training on a larger dataset.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Loss baselines:** Compare the initial objective to a simple expected baseline rather than assuming any decreasing number is good.
  - Example: For a balanced K-class task, compare initial cross-entropy with log(K).
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.
      - Watch for: Focus on loss baselines. Then reproduce the lesson example: For a balanced K-class task, compare initial cross-entropy with log(K).
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Gradient and update checks:** A nonzero loss is not enough: parameters must receive finite gradients and actual updates.
  - Example: Record grad norm and parameter delta before and after one optimiser step.
  - Videos:
    - [Makemore: activations, gradients and BatchNorm](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P6sfmUTpUmc) · Andrej Karpathy · From-scratch lecture
      - Explains: Activation statistics, initialization problems, gradients and batch normalization.
      - Useful because: Debug vanishing/exploding behavior with measured statistics.
      - Watch for: Focus on gradient and update checks. Then reproduce the lesson example: Record grad norm and parameter delta before and after one optimiser step.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Numerical non-finites:** NaN and infinity can enter through invalid operations, unstable exponentials or exploding updates; find the first failing tensor.
  - Example: Inject log(0) into a toy graph and use finite checks to locate its origin.

### Profiling, batching, precision and portable model artifacts

Measure the actual serving bottleneck and package the preprocessing and model state needed to reproduce predictions.

**Priority:** Specialization · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [Mixed precision, memory and inference optimization](dl.md#dl-efficiency) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Warmup and measurement boundaries:** Initial setup and caching can distort timings; define whether a measurement includes preprocessing and queueing.
  - Example: Warm up a tiny CPU model, then time preprocessing, inference and total request work separately.
  - Videos:
    - [Mixed precision training from scratch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7NrYjhpiCY) · Vuk Rosić · Focused tutorial
      - Explains: FP16/BF16, autocast and gradient scaling in PyTorch.
      - Useful because: Understand the memory/stability tradeoff; follow the CPU lab if GPU support is unavailable.
      - Watch for: Focus on warmup and measurement boundaries. Then reproduce the lesson example: Warm up a tiny CPU model, then time preprocessing, inference and total request work separately.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7NrYjhpiCY
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on warmup and measurement boundaries. Then reproduce the lesson example: Warm up a tiny CPU model, then time preprocessing, inference and total request work separately.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Batch throughput versus latency:** Batching amortises overhead but waiting to fill a batch can increase individual request latency.
  - Example: Compare batch sizes one, eight and sixteen on the same 128 generated examples.
  - Videos:
    - [Mixed precision training from scratch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7NrYjhpiCY) · Vuk Rosić · Focused tutorial
      - Explains: FP16/BF16, autocast and gradient scaling in PyTorch.
      - Useful because: Understand the memory/stability tradeoff; follow the CPU lab if GPU support is unavailable.
      - Watch for: Focus on batch throughput versus latency. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare batch sizes one, eight and sixteen on the same 128 generated examples.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7NrYjhpiCY
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on batch throughput versus latency. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare batch sizes one, eight and sixteen on the same 128 generated examples.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Precision and hardware support:** Reduced precision is useful only where supported and accurate enough; CPU execution does not require a GPU mixed-precision lab.
  - Example: Keep the required baseline in float32 and inspect alternative dtype support before testing it.
  - Videos:
    - [Mixed precision training from scratch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7NrYjhpiCY) · Vuk Rosić · Focused tutorial
      - Explains: FP16/BF16, autocast and gradient scaling in PyTorch.
      - Useful because: Understand the memory/stability tradeoff; follow the CPU lab if GPU support is unavailable.

      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/

## Audio and multimodal learning

<a id="dl-audio-multimodal"></a>

### Audio sampling, spectrograms and multimodal fusion

Understand how non-text signals become model inputs and evaluate alignment before combining modalities.

**Priority:** Specialization · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [RNN/LSTM, attention and transformers](dl.md#dl-sequences) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Sampling rate and duration:** The number of audio samples depends on duration and sampling rate; changing metadata without resampling changes interpretation.
  - Example: Generate one second of a 440Hz sine wave at 16kHz and verify it contains 16000 samples.
  - Videos:
    - [MIT 6.S191 (2025) — Deep Sequence Modeling](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GvezxUdLrEk) · MIT · Alexander Amini · University lecture
      - Explains: Sequence representations and neural architectures for ordered inputs.
      - Useful because: Use the sequence-model framing alongside the recurrent and attention implementation exercises.
      - Watch for: Focus on sampling rate and duration. Then reproduce the lesson example: Generate one second of a 440Hz sine wave at 16kHz and verify it contains 16000 samples.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://introtodeeplearning.com/2025/index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on sampling rate and duration. Then reproduce the lesson example: Generate one second of a 440Hz sine wave at 16kHz and verify it contains 16000 samples.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Windows and spectrograms:** A short-time Fourier transform computes local frequency content using a window and hop length; a spectrogram trades time and frequency resolution.
  - Example: Compare two window sizes on generated tones and annotate the time/frequency axes.
  - Videos:
    - [MIT 6.S191 (2025) — Deep Sequence Modeling](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GvezxUdLrEk) · MIT · Alexander Amini · University lecture
      - Explains: Sequence representations and neural architectures for ordered inputs.
      - Useful because: Use the sequence-model framing alongside the recurrent and attention implementation exercises.
      - Watch for: Focus on windows and spectrograms. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare two window sizes on generated tones and annotate the time/frequency axes.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://introtodeeplearning.com/2025/index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on windows and spectrograms. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compare two window sizes on generated tones and annotate the time/frequency axes.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Mel scaling and log values:** Mel filterbanks group frequencies using a perceptual scale, and log energy needs a safe floor for silence.
  - Example: Compute a mel spectrogram for a synthetic signal and verify a silent input produces finite log values.
  - Videos:
    - [MIT 6.S191 (2025) — Deep Sequence Modeling](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GvezxUdLrEk) · MIT · Alexander Amini · University lecture
      - Explains: Sequence representations and neural architectures for ordered inputs.
      - Useful because: Use the sequence-model framing alongside the recurrent and attention implementation exercises.
      - Watch for: Focus on mel scaling and log values. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compute a mel spectrogram for a synthetic signal and verify a silent input produces finite log values.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://introtodeeplearning.com/2025/index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on mel scaling and log values. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compute a mel spectrogram for a synthetic signal and verify a silent input produces finite log values.

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Early versus late fusion:** Modalities can be combined at feature level or after separate predictions, but their sample identity and timing must agree.
  - Example: Join a tiny audio-feature table with text labels by a stable sample ID and detect one mismatched pair.
  - Videos:

## Reinforcement learning overview

<a id="dl-reinforcement-basics"></a>

### Rewards, policies, value estimates and exploration

Distinguish reward-based decision learning from ordinary tool orchestration before choosing a reinforcement-learning approach.

**Priority:** Specialization · **Study:** 3h · **Practice:** 4h

**Prerequisites:** [Supervised learning, regression and classification](ml.md#ml-problem) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **States, actions and transitions:** A sequential decision problem specifies what is observed, which actions are allowed and how the environment changes.
  - Example: Define a three-state toy environment with two actions and explicit terminal transitions.
  - Videos:
    - [MIT 6.S191 (2025) — Deep Reinforcement Learning](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=to-lHJfK4pw) · MIT · Alexander Amini · University lecture
      - Explains: Decision-making with rewards, policies and reinforcement-learning methods.
      - Useful because: Build vocabulary before a small bandit experiment; large-scale agent training is optional.
      - Watch for: Focus on states, actions and transitions. Then reproduce the lesson example: Define a three-state toy environment with two actions and explicit terminal transitions.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://introtodeeplearning.com/2025/index.html
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on states, actions and transitions. Then reproduce the lesson example: Define a three-state toy environment with two actions and explicit terminal transitions.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Reward and return:** Immediate rewards differ from discounted future return, and reward design determines what behaviour is incentivised.
  - Example: Calculate the discounted sum for a short reward sequence at two discount factors.
  - Videos:
    - [MIT 6.S191 (2025) — Deep Reinforcement Learning](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=to-lHJfK4pw) · MIT · Alexander Amini · University lecture

      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.

      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Policy versus value:** A policy chooses actions while a value estimate predicts expected return under specified assumptions.
  - Example: Represent an epsilon-greedy bandit policy separately from its action-value estimates.
  - Videos:
    - [MIT 6.S191 (2025) — Deep Reinforcement Learning](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=to-lHJfK4pw) · MIT · Alexander Amini · University lecture
      - Explains: Decision-making with rewards, policies and reinforcement-learning methods.

## Distributed training: ranks, synchronization and effective batches

<a id="dl-distributed-training"></a>

### Distributed training: ranks, synchronization and effective batches

Distributed training: ranks, synchronization and effective batches helps you make explainable engineering decisions and test failure cases. Build the experiment below before relying on the concept in an AI system.

**Priority:** Specialization · **Study:** 4h · **Practice:** 5h

**Prerequisites:** [PyTorch loops, checkpoints and reproducibility](dl.md#dl-training-loop) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Data parallelism:** Each worker holds a model copy and processes a different shard before gradients are combined.
  - Example: Split eight samples into two four-sample shards and compare averaged gradients.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on data parallelism. Then reproduce the lesson example: Split eight samples into two four-sample shards and compare averaged gradients.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Ranks and world size:** Ranks identify workers and world size counts participating processes.
  - Example: Label two CPU worker fixtures as ranks zero and one.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on ranks and world size. Then reproduce the lesson example: Label two CPU worker fixtures as ranks zero and one.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Gradient synchronization:** Workers must agree on parameter updates to keep replicated models consistent.
  - Example: Average two gradient vectors and apply the same update to both model copies.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on gradient synchronization. Then reproduce the lesson example: Average two gradient vectors and apply the same update to both model copies.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Effective batch size:** Per-worker batch size, worker count and accumulation determine samples per update.
  - Example: Compute 4 samples times 2 workers times 3 accumulation steps.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h
      - Explains: Tensors, training workflows, classification, computer vision and model experiments.
      - Useful because: A long hands-on course: study the relevant workflow, then build a small CPU lab.
      - Watch for: Focus on effective batch size. Then reproduce the lesson example: Compute 4 samples times 2 workers times 3 accumulation steps.
      - Free YouTube video; no purchase required. Promoted tools/certificates may be paid. Use local labs and current linked documentation.
      - Verification source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-pytorch-for-deep-learning-in-day/
- [ ] **Distributed failure modes:** A missing worker or inconsistent collective order can stall training.
  - Example: Model a timed-out worker in a deterministic coordinator simulation.
  - Videos:
    - [PyTorch for deep learning — full course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_xro1bcAuA) · freeCodeCamp · Daniel Bourke · Long course · approximately 26h

## Profiling, memory bandwidth and kernel optimization decisions

<a id="dl-kernel-profiling"></a>

### Profiling, memory bandwidth and kernel optimization decisions

Profiling, memory bandwidth and kernel optimization decisions helps you make explainable engineering decisions and test failure cases. Build the experiment below before relying on the concept in an AI system.

**Priority:** Specialization · **Study:** 4h · **Practice:** 5h

**Prerequisites:** [Profiling, batching, precision and portable model artifacts](dl.md#dl-profiling-deployment) Navigation is unrestricted.

#### Concepts

- [ ] **Measurement boundaries:** Warmup, synchronization and repeated trials affect valid performance measurements.
  - Example: Measure median runtime after warmup and separate setup from repeated inference.
  - Videos:
    - [Mixed precision training from scratch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C7NrYjhpiCY) · Vuk Rosić · Focused tutorial

## Stage checkpoint

<a id="checkpoint-dl"></a>

### Foundation capstone: classical versus neural models

Demonstrate readiness through a reproducible practical handoff. Use bundled digits to compare a dummy baseline, logistic regression, a tree model and a small PyTorch network on identical splits. Explain gradients, loss, optimizer and tensor shapes. Save artifacts, reproduce inference, report errors and CPU latency, and document limitations.

**Priority:** Foundation · **Study:** 1h · **Practice:** 18h

**Prerequisites:** [Tensors, shapes, networks and autograd](dl.md#dl-tensors), [Sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, GELU and softmax](dl.md#dl-activations), [MSE, binary and multiclass cross-entropy](dl.md#dl-losses), [SGD, momentum, RMSprop, Adam and AdamW](dl.md#dl-optimizers), [Learning rates, schedules, batch sizes and initialization](dl.md#dl-training-settings), [Dropout, normalization, clipping and early stopping](dl.md#dl-regularization), [PyTorch loops, checkpoints and reproducibility](dl.md#dl-training-loop), [CNNs and transfer learning](dl.md#dl-cnn), [RNN/LSTM, attention and transformers](dl.md#dl-sequences), [Tensor indexing, broadcasting and memory layout](dl.md#dl-shape-algebra), [Gradients, computation graphs and gradient checking](dl.md#dl-gradient-mechanics), [Initialisation, signal scale and residual connections](dl.md#dl-initialization-depth), [Datasets, DataLoader, collation and padding](dl.md#dl-data-pipeline), [SGD, Adam bias correction and decoupled weight decay](dl.md#dl-adamw-math), [Learning-rate schedules, effective batch size and experiments](dl.md#dl-learning-rate-experiments), [BatchNorm, LayerNorm, dropout and train/eval modes](dl.md#dl-normalization-modes), [Log-sum-exp, cross-entropy gradients and label semantics](dl.md#dl-loss-derivatives), [Convolutions, padding, stride, dilation and pooling](dl.md#dl-convolution-arithmetic), [Transfer learning, augmentation and frozen backbones](dl.md#dl-transfer-augmentation), [RNN, LSTM, GRU and teacher forcing](dl.md#dl-recurrent-state), [Queries, keys, values, masks and multi-head attention](dl.md#dl-attention-math), [Transformer blocks, positions and encoder/decoder tasks](dl.md#dl-transformer-blocks), [Overfit one batch, diagnose loss and debug numerical failures](dl.md#dl-training-diagnostics) Navigation is unrestricted.
